Welcome to Xsegon

Xsegon shows your games like a console menu and starts them for you. It is made for a TV and a controller, and it is just as happy with a keyboard and mouse. Thanks for giving it a go.

For Xsegon v0.18, October 2026. It is an early version, so if something acts up, that is normal. Nothing you do in it can harm your games.

There is nothing to fill in and nothing you have to do. Set it up, play some games, poke around. Further down are the five things most worth trying, and the new ones to play with. If you feel like telling me how it went, the last part says how. Click any picture to see it bigger.

Had the last version? This is what is new.

  • Setting up is one window. Set everything up shows the folder your games are in and a switch for each part, and one press does the rest.
  • New games come in by themselves. Put games in your games folder, come back to Xsegon, and they are there.
  • A game's pictures and video in one tab. A game's new Media tab shows them: change any of them, clear them, or copy another game's onto it.
  • The menus on every screen. Press the Xsegon logo at the top left.
  • RetroArch comes with it. Setting up no longer downloads 200 MB first: only the cores your consoles need are fetched.
  • Coming from LaunchBox? Games > Bring in a LaunchBox library... brings your games and your own play data across, once.
  • Install and bonus discs go with their game, in its new Accompanied files tab, and are no longer taken for games.
  • Connect a phone works in the download now.

This version sets itself up in its own folder, and the older one is left as it was.

1What you need

  • A PC with Windows 10 or 11. Xsegon opens in Chrome or Edge, and Edge is already on Windows.
  • Your own game files. Xsegon does not come with any games.
  • About 2 GB of free space, and the internet for the first few minutes.
  • A controller, if you have one. It works as soon as you press a button on it.

2Start it

  1. Right-click the zip, choose Extract All..., and put it somewhere simple, like Documents.
  2. Open the folder it made and double-click Start Xsegon.bat.
  3. If Windows says "Windows protected your PC", press More info, then Run anyway. It says that because Xsegon is home-made, not because anything is wrong.

Xsegon opens full screen. To close it, use the X at its top right (it asks first), or press Alt+F4.

If double-clicking does nothing at all: right-click the zip, choose Properties, select Unblock at the bottom, press OK, and unzip it again. If the last version is still open, close that one first.

3Let it set itself up

The first time, Xsegon opens one window, Set everything up. One press and you are playing:

  1. Your games. If Xsegon already sees your games, it names the folder and how many there are. If not, press Pick the folder... and choose the folder your games are in. Any folder works: Xsegon looks inside every folder under it.
  2. What Xsegon sets up. A switch for each part, with what it takes beside it: names and box art, adding new games by themselves, videos for your games, the cheat lists, and a games check that opens each game for a moment to see that it starts. Everything is on but the games check. None of them is needed to play, and each can be had later from the menus.
  3. Press Set it up. Nothing more is asked.

Then leave it to it. A small list in the bottom corner shows what it is doing: setting up RetroArch (the program that plays the games, which comes with Xsegon), finding your games, and fetching their names and box art. When the list says Ready to play, you are. That takes about a minute on a fast connection and a few minutes on a slow one, and you can look around while it works. Videos, if you left them on, keep coming in for a few minutes after that.

Rather go step by step? Set up by hand opens Getting started: every step, one at a time, with a button for each. Help > Getting started opens it again any time.

Not sure where to put your games? Xsegon made a Games folder beside itself, with a folder inside for each console. Press Set it up anyway: Xsegon sets up the rest, then says where that folder is, with a button that opens it. Drop your games in, come back to Xsegon, and they come in by themselves.

4Getting around

You start on your consoles. Turn to one and open it to see its games.

ToKeyboardController
MoveThe arrow keysThe cross or the left stick
Open a console, or play a gameEnterA
Go backEscB
See a game's own pageSpaceX
A game's menuRight-clickY
Find a game/ and a few letters
Change how the games are shownG
Stop playing a gameEsc, in the game

You do not have to remember any of it: the bar along the bottom of the screen always shows what the keys do right now, and with a controller it shows that controller's own buttons. With a mouse, click a game to choose it, click it again for its page, and right-click it for its menu.

The menus (Games, Emulators, Help) and Get Media open from the Xsegon logo at the top left, on every screen, with Xsegon's own beneath them: Settings, the controller, Connect a phone and the themes. In the List, Grid and Shelf looks the menus also stand along the top, with View, and the logo is the round X beside them. Settings is always the button at the top right.

5The five things most worth trying

If you only do a little, do these. They are the ones I most want to hear about.

  1. Play a few games, from different consoles. Choose one and press Enter. Esc in the game brings you back to Xsegon, on the same game.
  2. Save, leave, and pick up where you left off. In a game, F2 saves where you are. Next time you press Play, Xsegon asks: a fresh start, or which save?
  3. Do it all with a controller. Press any button on it, then put the keyboard aside. The bar at the bottom names your controller's own buttons: A and B on an Xbox pad, the shapes on a PlayStation pad. I have only ever tried an Xbox one, so a PlayStation or Nintendo pad is the one I am most curious about.
  4. Close it and start it again. It should come back just as you left it.
  5. See it on the TV, if your PC reaches one. That is where it is meant to live. Plug the TV in while Xsegon is open and it draws itself again for the bigger screen, in a couple of seconds.

6New things to play with

A game's pictures and video in one tabnew

A game's page has a new Media tab, right after About. It opens on what the game shows: a row for each picture (box art, 3D box, clear logo, screenshot, fanart) and one for the video. Press a picture for what Change Pictures offers for it (replace it, find one online, or reset it), or drop a picture file on it. Press the video to clear it.

Copy from another game... lists the games in your library that have pictures or a video, the same console's first, with a box to find one by name. Press a game to see its pictures and video beside this game's own, then press a row to copy that one, or Copy all it has. Handy for a second copy of a game that should look like the first.

New games come in by themselvesnew

Put games in your games folder, come back to Xsegon, and they are there. When Xsegon starts, and when its window comes back to the front after a while away, it looks in your games folders and adds the new games it is sure of, naming them on the strip at the bottom. Anything it is not sure of (a possible hack, a disc set waiting for its playlist) waits for Games > Scan for Games. It is a switch in Set everything up, and in Settings > Library.

Your games on your phone

Sit on the sofa, look through your games on your phone, tap one, and it starts on the PC.

  1. Press the Xsegon logo at the top left (in List or Grid, the round X) and choose Connect a phone...
  2. Press Switch on. Windows asks once whether to allow it: say Yes.
  3. A square appears. Point the phone's camera at it and tap the link it shows.
  4. Your games are on the phone. Tap one, then Play on the TV.

The phone has to be on the same Wi-Fi as the PC. Nothing is installed on it, and next time it only has to open its bookmark. A phone can see your games and start one, and nothing else.

Videos for your games

A short video of each game, from free online archives, for far more consoles than before, and for arcade games too. If you did not select them during setup: Get Media > Videos from online archives..., then Start. The window closes and a bar in the corner shows how far it is. Stay on a game for a moment and its video plays.

Themes that move

Press the Xsegon logo (in List or Grid, the round X): under Themes there are folders. Space has a sky of drifting stars, with one falling now and then, and the same sky over a wood of firs. Nature has the Deep sea with its bubbles, a Storm, and Winter with snow. Neon has Matrix and Synthwave. Carbon has embers, and in the Dracula ones a bat crosses the screen every minute or two. Xsegon theme goes back to how it came.

Cheats in one press

A game's page has a Cheats tab. If you did not select the cheat lists during setup, the tab offers Get the cheat lists...: press it, press Download, and a bar in the corner shows them coming in (about 35 MB). Then select a cheat and it is on, every time you play that game.

And a few more

  • Find games faster. The funnel in the search box opens Filter by: favourites, never played, your own rating, and more. A small x on the funnel clears them again.
  • The List, your way. In the List look, press the three-lines button at the right-hand end of the headers to choose your columns. Drag a header to move it, drag its edge to resize it, and right-click it for more. With Your rating showing, you can give stars right in a game's row.
  • Pick which version plays. A game you have twice (USA and Europe, say) is one card with a small stack mark. On its page, the Versions tab lets you select the one Play starts.
  • See your controller light up. Settings > Xsegon Controls > Controller check draws your controller and lights each button as you press it. With none plugged in, it says so. Xsegon's buttons, on the same page, lets you choose what each button does.
  • Clear a video, or every picture. Right-click a game > Replace Video... has Clear video..., and Change Pictures has Clear all..., and each window says first what goes.
  • ScreenScraper videos with a free account. Get Media > ScreenScraper videos asks only for the name and password of a free screenscraper.fr account.
  • One set of keyboard keys for every console. Settings > RetroArch + Emulator Controls > RetroArch (Keyboard) opens on Every console: a key set there is set for all of them at once.
  • And the old favourites. Six looks (G), favourites and stars, a Notes tab on every game's page, and R for a game picked for you.

7If something goes wrong

  • Stuck somewhere? Press Esc a few times. It always backs out one step.
  • Still stuck? Close Xsegon and start it again. Nothing is lost: it keeps everything as you go.
  • Games with names but no pictures? Choose List or Grid, then Get Media > Get Pictures.
  • Pictures slow to appear in the Grid? Settings > Library > Thumbnail cache > Build thumbs makes small copies of them, once.
  • A game will not start? A red line at the bottom says why. A few consoles (the PlayStation is one) need a BIOS file of your own: Emulators > BIOS check says which one and where it goes. Xsegon never downloads one.
  • A controller that works in Xsegon and not in a game? The Controller check has Wrong in a game?, which says what to do.
  • The phone cannot open the link? It has to be on the same Wi-Fi as the PC, and Windows has to have been told Yes. The Connect a phone window says what Windows allows, and how to put it right.
  • Xsegon will not open at all? A black window comes up and says why. A photo of it, sent to help@tumultuousproductions.site, is all I need.

8Tell me what you think, if you feel like it

No homework. If something annoyed you, confused you or made you smile, a line or two to help@tumultuousproductions.site is perfect. "It all worked" is good to hear too. And if you used a PlayStation or Nintendo controller, or opened your games on a phone, I would love to know how that went.

If something broke and you would like to help me fix it, Xsegon can pack what happened into one small file:

Settings > Debug > Report a problem... > Make a report > Save a copy

It lands in your Downloads folder as xsegon-report with the date. Send it to help@tumultuousproductions.site, with a line or two about what you were doing. It holds Xsegon's own record of what happened, your settings and the names of your games. Your games themselves, your pictures and your videos are never in it.

Good to know

  • Your game files are only ever read. Xsegon never changes or moves them.
  • Everything Xsegon makes lives inside the folder you unzipped. To remove it, close Xsegon and delete that folder. Nothing is installed anywhere else.
  • After the first setup it works without the internet. Only fetching pictures, videos and cheat lists needs it.

Click anywhere or press Esc to close.
